deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from §2 on the previous pages). X is a topological space and X = ⊔_{i∈I} X_i is a finite partition into 'leaves' (feuilles). It is called a cellular decomposition (décomposition cellulaire) when it satisfies three conditions. (1) Frontier condition: each closure \bar X_i is a union of leaves. (2) Distinct leaves have distinct closures. (3) Each leaf is minimal in the Boolean-type family F_p generated by the partition. The previous page proves 1)+2) ⇔ 3) and sets up the quotient Y = X/R ≅ I, a finite topological space.

This page gives a dictionary between such decompositions and finite quotient spaces.
- Closed sets of I correspond to closed saturated subsets of X, i.e. closed unions of leaves.
- The closure of {i} in I is the smallest closed set of I containing i. It corresponds to the smallest closed saturated subset of X containing X_i. By (1), that is \bar X_i itself.
- Hence j ∈ \bar{{i}} ⇔ X_j ⊂ \bar X_i ⇔ \bar X_j ⊂ \bar X_i. So the incidence relation of the cells is exactly the specialization preorder of the finite space I.
- Condition (2), \bar X_i = \bar X_j ⇒ i = j, says that \bar{{i}} = \bar{{j}} ⇒ i = j. Grothendieck calls this 'pré-sobre'; it is the T0 / Kolmogorov axiom. For finite spaces it is equivalent to sobriety, so I is a finite poset with its Alexandrov topology.
- With φ: X → I the quotient map, condition (1) says that J ↦ φ^{-1}(J) commutes with closure (equivalently with interior). For a continuous map this is equivalent to φ being open.

Conclusion stated on the page: finite cellular decompositions of X correspond bijectively to finite quotients X → X/R that are T0 ('présobres') and whose quotient map is open. In modern terms: finite stratifications satisfying the frontier condition are the same as continuous open surjections X → P onto a finite poset with the Alexandrov topology.

§3 then begins, under the heading 'Décompositions cellulaires F-admissibles'. Here F ⊂ P(X) is the family of admissible ('tame') subsets axiomatized in §1. A cellular decomposition is called F-admissible if its leaves belong to F, i.e. F_p ⊂ F. The next page proves existence of a coarsest F-admissible cellular decomposition refining a given finite family L ⊂ F. The proof uses rare (nowhere dense) boundaries and induction on a smaller closed set.

The page serves Grothendieck's axiomatic 'topologie modérée': a tame family F of subsets, and stratifications (dévissages) adapted to it.
errors: No mathematical error. The equivalence 'φ continuous is open ⇔ φ^{-1} commutes with closure' is a standard fact and is correctly applied.
'Pré-sobre' is used for T0. For finite spaces T0 ⇔ sober, so no harm, but the term is non-standard.

Surjectivity and finiteness of I, and continuity of φ, are implicit (φ is the quotient map). The bijection is between decompositions and isomorphism classes of such quotients; this is not spelled out but is evident.

ideas.what: The incidence relation among cells of a stratification equals the specialization order of the finite quotient space X/R.
ideas.modern_name: Stratification as a continuous map to a poset with the Alexandrov topology; poset of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore. Finite T0 spaces ↔ posets: Alexandroff (1937), McCord (1966). Stratifications as maps to Alexandrov posets: popularized by Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A, c. 2011-17), also Treumann, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 discusses tame stratifications in general terms, but not, as far as I know, this formulation.

ideas.what: Finite cellular decompositions (frontier condition plus distinct closures) ↔ finite T0 quotients X → X/R with open quotient map.
ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition ⇔ the stratification map X → P is open (for finite P)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in the stratified-spaces literature (e.g. Lurie HA A.5; later work by Haine, Douteau, Waas and others on poset-stratified spaces); no clear single attribution.

ideas.what: Definition of F-admissible cellular decompositions (leaves belong to the tame family F), as a preliminary to the existence of a coarsest admissible decomposition refining a finite family.
ideas.modern_name: Stratification adapted to (compatible with) a family of definable sets, in an axiomatic tame setting
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s); Whitney/Thom/Mather stratifications compatible with subsets.
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic mention in Esquisse §5-6 (1984).

missed.claim: In 1974 Grothendieck explicitly identifies finite stratifications with the frontier condition with open continuous maps onto finite T0 (pré-sobre) spaces, i.e. finite posets. The incidence relation is identified with the specialization order. This is the now-standard 'stratification = map to a poset' viewpoint, together with the characterization of the frontier condition as openness of the map.
missed.quote: les décompositions cellulaires (finies) X correspondent aux espaces quotients finis de X qui sont présobres, et tels que X → X/R soit ouverte
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This viewpoint underlies the modern theory of poset-stratified spaces (exit-path ∞-categories, constructible sheaves). The page shows Grothendieck had the formulation, including the openness/frontier-condition link, some decades before it became standard. That is a historical priority point rather than a new theorem.

missed.claim: An axiomatic tame family F (§1, conditions a-e) is used to define admissible cellular decompositions, aiming at existence of a canonical coarsest admissible decomposition. This is a model-theory-free axiomatization of tame topology predating o-minimality. It is the concrete content of the 'topologie modérée' programme only sketched in the Esquisse.
missed.quote: une décomposition cellulaire de X est dite F-admissible ... si ses feuilles sont ∈ F, i.e. si F_p ⊂ F
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparing Grothendieck's §1 axioms with o-minimal structures and with recent 'tame geometry' axiomatics could clarify what minimal axioms suffice for canonical stratifications.

deep.surprise_reason: The dictionary (stratifications with frontier condition ↔ open maps to finite T0 spaces) is elementary and folklore today. Its explicit appearance in 1974 notes within an axiomatic tame-topology framework is a nice unpublished detail and an early instance of the poset-stratification viewpoint, but not a deep new result.
